pathway.name: Introduction to the BC Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act
pathway.description: Learners will have an increased understanding of the content, purpose and government commitments related to the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act and Action Plan.

bookmarks.title: A collaborative process
bookmarks.description: This activity is a video with speakers share their voices about working together to meet government commitments.

bookmarks.title: The Declaration Act Secretariat
bookmarks.description: Learners will become familiar with the function, role and purpose of the Secretariat in implementing the Action Plan.

bookmarks.title: The Annual Report
bookmarks.description: Learners will understand the purpose of the annual report and the importance of the report to action plan implementation.

bookmarks.title: Alignment of laws
bookmarks.description: Learners will have a better understanding of what it means to align laws and how the Province of BC is approaching the alignment of legislation with the Declaration Act

bookmarks.title: Implementing the Declaration Act
bookmarks.description: Learners will have a deeper understanding of how the Declaration Act is being implemented through the action plan and the Secretariat.

bookmarks.title: A distinctions based approach
bookmarks.description: Learn about the distinction-based approach for the way the Province conducts  work with First Nations, Métis, and Inuit people.

bookmarks.title: All the details- Ministry of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation
bookmarks.description: Learners will have access to all the specific details about the Action plan directly form the Ministry of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation

bookmarks.title: Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act Action Plan
bookmarks.description: The Action Plan outlines goals and outcomes for ending Indigenous-specific racism and discrimination in British Columbia.

bookmarks.title: The Declaration Act Secretariat
bookmarks.description: Learners will become familiar with the function, role and purpose of the Secretariat in implementing the Action Plan.

bookmarks.title: The Action Plan Announcement
bookmarks.description: This article introduces BC's announcement of the Action Plan.

bookmarks.title: Calls to Action- why are they important?
bookmarks.description: This activity will strengthen learners understanding of the Truth and Reconciliation Calls to Action, and why they are so important.

bookmarks.title: 94 calls to action
bookmarks.description: This activity allows learners to see all the Calls to Action  from the Truth and Reconciliation commission final report.

bookmarks.title: Decolonizing Reconciliation
bookmarks.description: Podcast- Telling Our Twisted Histories. An episode about Reconciliation.

steps.name: The UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples

bookmarks.title: The UN Declaration
bookmarks.description: Learners can review the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples in its entirety in this activity.

bookmarks.title: How UNDRIP changes the relationship with Indigenous peoples
bookmarks.description: This activity provides context and an explanation as to why the UN Declaration is so important, and how it changes the way the world must engage with Indigenous peoples.

bookmarks.title: Implementing the UN Declaration through Bill C-15
bookmarks.description: This activity will provide learners with context regarding Bill C-15 and when it came to be.

bookmarks.title: How much do you know about the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People?
bookmarks.description: This activity includes resources to support learners in developing their competency and knowledge about the rights of Indigenous people. The quiz on this activity is broken but the resources on this website are valuable.

steps.name: The Draft 10 principles that Guide the Province of British Columbias Relationship with Indigenous People

bookmarks.title: The Draft 10 Principles
bookmarks.description: Learners will have the opportunity to read the Draft 10 Principles document in its entirety.

bookmarks.title: Draft 10 Principle FAQs
bookmarks.description: Learners will be able to review frequently asked questions about the 10 Draft Principles to answer potential questions they may have and to deepen their understanding.

bookmarks.title: Proposed Commitment Document 2015
bookmarks.description: Learners will have the opportunity to read the Commitment Document setting out a proposed joint agenda and action plan for significant work to be done between First nation and BC and the Provincial Government.

bookmarks.title: Concrete Actions: Transforming Laws,  Policies, Processes  and Structures
bookmarks.description: Learners will read through the The Commitment Document which sets out a proposed implementation and engagement process which includes First Nations engagement, BC Government engagement, Business and Industry Engagement, Federal Government Engagement, and Public Awareness and Other Stakeholders.

steps.name: Engagement with Indigenous Peoples, Organizations and Communities

bookmarks.title: First Nation Community Engagement (ictinc.ca)
bookmarks.description: This is a blog about effective, respectful and consistent engagement with First Nation communities and working effectively with Indigenous Peoples.

bookmarks.title: Principles Respecting the Government of Canada's Relationship with Indigenous Peoples (justice.gc.ca)
bookmarks.description: This is an article on the principles of respecting the Government of Canada's relationship with Indigenous Peoples including a poster with these principles.

bookmarks.title: Community Engagement Fatigue when Working with Small, Hard to Reach and/or Indigenous Communities
bookmarks.description: This is a YouTube video of Jennifer Franks Lead, Indigenous Placemaking, City of Toronto, speaking to empathizing and strategizing community engagement fatigue when working with small, hard to reach and/or Indigenous communities.

bookmarks.title: Indigenous Planning: Six Examples of Creative Engagement that Work (Sharedvaluesolutions.com)
bookmarks.description: This article by Jessica Steiner and Laura Taylor is about Indigenous planning, including six examples of creative engagement that work.

bookmarks.title: Consultation Guide (C-Guide)
bookmarks.description: This is the government's source of guidance, resources, and tools respecting the Province's obligation to consult and accommodate First Nations. C-guide is maintained by Strategic Consultation Initiatives, Ministry of Indigenous Relations and Reconciliation.
